{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

#FLUX --job-name=BlokusGreedyNoDiscount
#FLUX --account=project_2010270
#FLUX --time=03:00:00
#FLUX --queue=medium
#FLUX --output={name}/simulate_{id}.out
#FLUX --error={name}/simulate_{id}.err

# NOTE: The --mail-type directive has been omitted as Flux does not have a direct
# equivalent for job status email notifications.

# Reserve compute
#FLUX --cpus-per-task=128
#FLUX --nodes=10
#FLUX --ntasks=10

# Print all arguments
echo "All arguments: $@"

# NOTE: This job appears to require GPUs (it installs tensorflow[and-cuda]) but does not
# explicitly request them from the scheduler. It is highly recommended to add a GPU request,
# for example: #FLUX --gpus-per-task=1

module purge
module load tensorflow/2.15

# The SLURM_JOB_NAME variable is replaced with the Flux equivalent.
mkdir -p $FLUX_JOB_NAME

echo "Job name: "$FLUX_JOB_NAME

RLF_BLOCKUS_SCRATCH="/scratch/project_2010270/"$FLUX_JOB_NAME

PIP_EXE=./venv/bin/pip3
PYTHON_EXE=./venv/bin/python3

if [ ! -d ./venv ]; then
    python3 -m venv venv
    source ./venv/bin/activate
    $PIP_EXE install --upgrade pip
    $PIP_EXE install --extra-index-url https://pypi.nvidia.com tensorrt-bindings==8.6.1 tensorrt-libs==8.6.1 tensorflow[and-cuda]==2.15
    $PIP_EXE install -e ./RLFramework
fi

source ./venv/bin/activate

which python3
which pip3
nvidia-smi

PYTHON_EXE=./venv/bin/python3

# Show information about the environment:
$PYTHON_EXE -c "import tensorflow as tf; print(tf.__version__)"
$PYTHON_EXE -c "import tensorflow as tf; print(tf.config.list_physical_devices('GPU'))"
$PYTHON_EXE --version

DATA_FOLDER=$RLF_BLOCKUS_SCRATCH/Data
MODEL_FOLDER=$RLF_BLOCKUS_SCRATCH/Models

rm -r $DATA_FOLDER

mkdir -p $DATA_FOLDER
mkdir -p $MODEL_FOLDER

if [ ! -e ./$FLUX_JOB_NAME/Blockus ]; then
    echo Copying Blokus Python folder to ./$FLUX_JOB_NAME/Blockus
    cp -r ./Blockus ./$FLUX_JOB_NAME/Blockus
fi

# NOTE: The original script's logic of iterating over the nodelist and launching
# a separate `srun` for each node is not the standard way to run a multi-node
# job. A single `flux run` command is used here to launch one task on each of
# the 10 allocated nodes. This assumes the Python script is written to handle
# the parallel execution, potentially using an environment variable like
# FLUX_NODEID to create its unique data folder.

# A simplified, more standard launch command:
flux run -n 10 --tasks-per-node=1 $PYTHON_EXE ./$FLUX_JOB_NAME/Blockus/only_simulate.py \
    --folder=$DATA_FOLDER'/$HOSTNAME' \
    --model_base_folder=$MODEL_FOLDER \
    --num_games=10000 \
    --num_cpus=120 \
    --num_files=-1

"
}
